title: Functional Browser
bodyHtml:
Explore interactive visualizations of dynamic perifusion assays, which show how islets from 413 human donors secrete insulin and glucagon over time upon exposure to a sequence of stimulatory and inhibitory conditions.

The analysis of data from these assays produces both normalized secretion values for each time point across baseline glucose, high glucose, high glucose plus IBMX, low glucose plus adrenaline, and KCl-induced depolarization exposures, as well as measures such as area under the curve (AUC) derived from these normalized values. Details on the processing of perifusion data and descriptions of the exposures and derived measures are here. To view processed experimental data and derived measures for individual donors, visit the Data Library.

The perifusion trace tab provides plots of normalized insulin and glucagon secretion across the exposure time course. By default, 95% confidence intervals are shown for all donors with data at each time point. See individual traces for all donors by choosing ‘Individual donors’. Hover over the plots to see individual donor traces. Select subsets of donors using filters on the left side. Alternatively, see results for selected donor IDs using the "Select donors" tab. Select "Copy link to results" to save your filtering criteria.

The 'Functional trait’ tabs view the relationship between derived measures such as AUC and different metadata fields. Select "Functional data by trait" for violin plots of derived measures stratified by a selected categorical field. Select “Functional data associations” to view a table of the association of a selected metadata field with each derived measure using linear regression models.

For interpretation and literature support of these functional data, visit the PanKgraph Functional Tool.
